questions.q: An engineer runs `aws s3 ls` on a laptop with a configured `dev` profile, but results come from the wrong account. A previous session exported `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` for another account. Why does this happen?

options.t: The credentials file always wins over the profile
options.why: Wrong: the credentials file is far down the precedence list.

options.t: Environment variables rank above the credentials file and config profile, so they override it
options.why: Right: order is CLI options, env vars, assume role, web identity, SSO, credentials file, and so on.

options.t: The CLI picks the most recently created key
options.why: Wrong: the CLI uses a fixed precedence order, not key age.

options.t: CloudTrail redirects calls to the last used account
options.why: Wrong: CloudTrail only records calls; it never routes them.

questions.explain: Env vars override profiles and instance roles; unset them and check with `aws configure list`.
questions.remember: Wrong account or surprise AccessDenied from the CLI → leftover env-var keys override the profile. Check `aws configure list` and `aws sts get-caller-identity`.
variants: Which identity am I using, with no permissions needed → `aws sts get-caller-identity`.
Also an explicit `--profile` flag → it beats env vars (CLI options rank first).

questions.q: Fifty engineers need terminal access to five AWS accounts. Security requires no long-term access keys, MFA through the corporate identity provider, and central control. Which approach fits?

options.t: One IAM user per engineer in each account with access keys rotated monthly
options.why: Wrong: long-term keys are the last resort and need per-account management.

options.t: A shared IAM user whose keys are stored in Secrets Manager
options.why: Wrong: shared long-term keys break traceability and are not short-lived.

options.t: Keys stored in `~/.aws/config` with `chmod 600`
options.why: Wrong: file permissions do not make keys short-lived or centrally controlled.

options.t: IAM Identity Center with `aws configure sso` profiles and `aws sso login`
options.why: Right: short-lived credentials, MFA via the identity provider, and central access across accounts.

questions.explain: IAM Identity Center gives short-lived, centrally managed CLI credentials.
questions.remember: Humans on the CLI across many accounts with no long-term keys → IAM Identity Center (SSO) profiles.
variants: Code running on EC2 → instance profile, no keys.
GitHub Actions deploying → OIDC web identity role.
On-premises server with X.509 certificates → IAM Roles Anywhere via `credential_process`.

questions.q: A GitHub Actions workflow must run `aws cloudformation deploy` against an account. The team will not store any AWS secrets in GitHub. What should be used?

options.t: An IAM user with keys saved as repository secrets
options.why: Wrong: that stores long-term keys.

options.t: An OIDC token exchanged through `AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity` for a role
options.why: Right: CI gets an OIDC token and receives temporary credentials, with no stored secrets.

options.t: An EC2 instance profile on the GitHub runner
options.why: Wrong: hosted runners are not your EC2 instances, so no instance profile exists.

options.t: `aws configure` with the root user keys
options.why: Wrong: root keys are the worst option and still long-term.

questions.explain: CI systems use web identity federation to get temporary role credentials.
questions.remember: CI/CD (GitHub, GitLab) calling AWS without stored secrets → OIDC web identity role.
variants: Pod on EKS needing AWS access → IRSA or Pod Identity (also web identity).

questions.q: A script runs `aws lambda invoke --function-name f --payload '{"k":"v"}' out.json` with CLI v2 and fails with an invalid base64 error. How do you fix it?

options.t: Switch the command to `aws lambda invoke-async`
options.why: Wrong: this does not address the encoding of the payload.

options.t: Add `--cli-binary-format raw-in-base64-out`
options.why: Right: CLI v2 expects base64 for blob parameters unless told the payload is raw text.

options.t: Add `--output text`
options.why: Wrong: output format does not change how the input is parsed.

options.t: Use `--no-paginate`
options.why: Wrong: pagination has nothing to do with the payload.

questions.explain: CLI v2 treats blobs as base64 by default; the flag allows raw JSON.
questions.remember: `Invalid base64` on a v2 call with a blob (Lambda payload, Kinesis data) → `--cli-binary-format raw-in-base64-out`.
variants: Passing JSON from a file → `file://`; binary from a file → `fileb://`.

questions.q: A script lists thousands of EC2 instances and only needs the IDs of running ones. The team wants the least data returned and cleanly parsable output in bash. Which is best?

options.t: `--query` with a JMESPath filter on the full response, output json
options.why: Wrong: `--query` filters on the client after the data is downloaded and gives no server-side reduction.

options.t: `--no-paginate` and pipe to `grep running`
options.why: Wrong: this returns only the first page and parses text unreliably.

options.t: `--page-size 1` with `--max-items 1`
options.why: Wrong: this returns almost nothing and does not filter.

options.t: `--filters Name=instance-state-name,Values=running` plus `--query` and `--output text`
options.why: Right: server-side filters reduce data, and `--query` with text output gives plain IDs for scripts.

questions.explain: Use server-side filters to cut data, `--query` plus `--output text` for scripting.
questions.remember: `--query` is client-side and does not cut API calls or cost; use `--filters`, `--prefix` or similar to reduce data server-side.
variants: DynamoDB scan with `--filter-expression` → still reads all items and uses capacity.
Capping total results → `--max-items` with `--starting-token` to continue.

questions.q: A nightly job syncs Airflow DAGs to the MWAA bucket with `aws s3 sync dags/ s3://mwaa-bucket/dags/ --delete`. After a path typo, many DAGs vanished. How should the team protect against this?

options.t: Replace `sync` with `aws s3 mv`
options.why: Wrong: `mv` copies then deletes the source, which is riskier.

options.t: Run with `--dryrun` first and enable bucket versioning for recovery
options.why: Right: `--dryrun` previews deletions and versioning makes them recoverable.

options.t: Remove `--delete` and `--exclude`, then use `cp --recursive`
options.why: Wrong: `cp` re-uploads everything and still does not prevent overwrites.

options.t: Increase `max_concurrent_requests`
options.why: Wrong: concurrency affects speed, not what is deleted.

questions.explain: `--delete` removes destination files absent from the source; test with `--dryrun`.
questions.remember: `s3 sync --delete` removes destination-only files → always `--dryrun` first and keep versioning on.
variants: Only new or changed files to upload → `sync` (size and modified time), not `cp --recursive`.
Filter order with `--exclude`/`--include` → later filters win.

questions.q: An EC2 instance in a private subnet with no internet route hangs on `aws s3 cp` and `aws glue get-tables`. The team wants no NAT gateway. What should they add?

options.t: `--no-verify-ssl` on every command
options.why: Wrong: this only affects TLS checks; the problem is the missing route.

options.t: A larger `multipart_chunksize`
options.why: Wrong: transfer tuning does not fix a missing route.

options.t: `--endpoint-url` pointing to the public endpoint
options.why: Wrong: the public endpoint is still unreachable without internet.

options.t: A gateway VPC endpoint for S3 and an interface endpoint for Glue
options.why: Right: gateway endpoints cover S3 and DynamoDB, interface endpoints cover most other services, and private DNS needs no `--endpoint-url`.

questions.explain: No route to the service endpoint means a VPC endpoint or NAT is needed.
questions.remember: CLI hangs in a private subnet → VPC endpoints (gateway for S3/DynamoDB, interface for the rest) or NAT; also check SGs, NACLs and proxy.
variants: Interface endpoint with private DNS on → normal hostnames resolve to it, so no `--endpoint-url`.

questions.q: Auditors ask which human ran a CLI command through a shared assumed role, and from where. What helps most?

options.t: CloudTrail events, using `role_session_name` set to the user's name and `sourceIPAddress`
options.why: Right: CloudTrail records every CLI call, and the session name and source IP identify the person.

options.t: The `~/.aws/cli/cache` files on the shared host
options.why: Wrong: the cache holds temporary tokens, not an audit trail, and is not centralized.

options.t: The `--debug` output of each command
options.why: Wrong: it is local, can leak secrets and is not an audit source.

options.t: `aws configure list`
options.why: Wrong: it shows local settings, not who ran past calls.

questions.explain: CloudTrail plus role session name and source IP gives traceability.
questions.remember: Who ran a CLI call as a role → CloudTrail: `userAgent` shows aws-cli, session name shows the person, `sourceIPAddress` the origin. Set `role_session_name`.
variants: Decode a long EC2 `UnauthorizedOperation` message → `aws sts decode-authorization-message`.
